espn-603993.headline: Argentina come to Dublin short of Carreras and a win
beats: Santiago Carreras, 70 Tests, limped off in the 13th minute for Bath and is out of the squad. Prop Thomas Gallo is also out with a wrist injury, and centre Santiago Chocobares is in doubt after a head knock. Carreras's place goes to Mateo Soler, who made his Test debut off the bench against Australia last month.
Argentina have not won since beating Wales in July. Three of the four games since were lost by seven points or fewer, and the fourth was a 28–28 draw with Australia.
Ireland have not played since conceding 40 away to New Zealand in July. They are third in the world, and an Argentina win would drop them below France.
Argentina have made a habit of losing by seven or fewer. In this competition that earns a bonus point. They need the four for a win.

sources.title: Argentina suffer injury blows ahead of Ireland game next week

espn-603994.headline: Italy's last home game ended with England beaten
beats: Since that 23–18 win over England in March, Italy have played four Tests, all away, and lost the lot. In July they conceded 47 to New Zealand and 57 to Australia a week apart.

South Africa lead the Nations Championship on points difference alone, level with New Zealand on 15. Their last outing was a 42–38 loss in Australia, and even a draw in Turin would drop them to second in the world, behind New Zealand.
Gonzalo Quesada calls Italy's position a "Situazione difficile". The cure on offer is a run of home Tests, starting here and then Argentina in Genoa a week later.
The last meeting, on 15 November 2025, was also in Italy, and South Africa won 32–14. Given how the year has gone, Italy would take an 18-point defeat as a decent afternoon.

sources.title: Nations Championship, Quesada alla vigilia delle gare di novembre: "Situazione difficile, ma che piacere ritrovarsi con staff e atleti, misureremo il valore del gruppo"

espn-603995.headline: Scotland have drawn twice with New Zealand. That is the peak
beats: This is the 34th meeting since the sides first met 111 years ago. New Zealand have won 31, Scotland none. Gregor Townsend lost 62-31 and 69-20 to them as a player and admits: "As a player, I don't think we ever felt we could win the game."

As coach he has lost three, all in Edinburgh, by five, eight and eight. Last November Scotland trailed 17-0, levelled at 17-17, and still lost 17-25. His verdict: "We might have lacked the composure."
New Zealand lost three straight to South Africa between late August and mid-September, then scored 50 and 43 against Australia. Scotland have not played since beating Fiji in July.
Win and Scotland go up to fifth in the world, above England. Australia come to Murrayfield a week later, though nobody in Edinburgh will be thinking that far ahead.

sources.title: Townsend never felt he could beat All Blacks as a player, but as a coach...

espn-603996.headline: One point in it last time, one point in it now
beats: Wales won the last meeting 24–23 in Cardiff on 15 November 2025. Four months earlier Japan had beaten them 24-19 in Kitakyushu, a defeat that stretched Wales's losing streak to 18 Tests.

Wales have not played since July, when South Africa beat them 43–0 a week after Argentina put 35 past them. Japan beat Fiji 20–15 to win the Pacific Nations Cup in September, then lost 28–34 to the same side at home on 24 October.

Wales sit a point clear of Japan in ninth in the Nations Championship. A Japan win lifts them above Wales and Italy in the world rankings and leaves Wales 12th at best, below the Italy side they beat in March.
A week later Wales host New Zealand and Japan go to England. Whoever loses here carries a bad week into a harder one.

sources.title: Wales losing streak up to 18 tests after losing to Japan in boiling Kitakyushu

espn-603997.headline: Eleven men down, and France start with Fiji
beats: France were already missing seven, Matthieu Jalibert and Thomas Ramos among them, when four more withdrew. Antoine Hastoy's ankle is one of them, and Castres fly-half Louis Le Brun comes in uncapped.
Fiji are bottom of the Nations Championship without a point. They come off a 34–28 win over Japan in Tokyo, a month after Japan beat them 20–15 in the Pacific Nations Cup final.
Any defeat costs France fourth place in the world, with South Africa in six days later. Their last meeting with Fiji, on 15 November 2025, finished 34–21 to France at home.
Fiji appointed Jake White in October. His last Test job ended in France in 2007, with the World Cup.

espn-603998.headline: Ten Tests since July meets a three-day camp
beats: England's last Test was a 31–24 win in Argentina on 18 July. Australia have played 10 since then, and Borthwick got a three-day camp at Bagshot before his players went back to their clubs.

Borthwick calls it "doing more of less". His fly-half may be doing less of everything: Fin Smith, who started at 10 in all three July Tests, damaged a calf, and Charlie Atkinson has been called up as cover.
Australia's extra miles have not all been happy ones. They beat South Africa 42–38, then conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand.
England won the last meeting 25–7 at home last November. Lose this one and they fall to seventh in the world, below Australia and Scotland, who host Australia a week later.
